revise.summary: I revised content/lessons/11-pr-and-ship.md and both gates now pass: the lint prints no ERROR lines (2,781 words) and the content test passed 14 tests. The chat Scene now has the agent rerun the tests, and its "before" is the failing run from earlier in the same test-first session, so the Evidence no longer comes from code the agent only read. The flow Scene now writes the body before the PR opens, which matches the chat Scene, the Try block and pr.md:35. Vercel previews are described per pushed branch, `/implement-spec`'s draft PR is marked ready at the end, and the Main flow step only applies when the work ships as a PR. Five quiz questions were rebuilt for transfer and single answers, and the repo-template question was reworded: scenario-review-effort (the high), body-only, spot-claim-evidence, spot-email-door, spot-merge-then-test, and a new sequence-review-body-ship that replaces sequence-ship. I added a clause at first use for each term a cold reader would trip on and cut repetition from Common mistakes. The Site story only says what the repo holds (the d21fc2c journal and PR bodies #2 to #9); PR #9's Evidence is now quoted word for word, and the story still doesn't claim `/pr` wrote it. I checked Matt's paraphrases from LlgiOCmFG_w against the English transcript on ai.engineer and the v1.3 changelog, and Discussion #835 and the Hacker News comment against their live pages.

quiz.where: Final test, spot-merge-then-test, stem "Why is that order risky?" (lines 429-437)
quiz.problem: This isn't a spot question. The stem already names the mistake (the order) and asks why it's risky. Two distractors then contradict the stem's own premise: a says "It isn't risky" and c says production waits, so the stem alone rules them out.
quiz.evidence: Line 429: "Sam clicks Squash and merge, then opens the preview to check the rename worked. Why is that order risky?" Line 430: "It isn't risky: a revert undoes a migration like any other change." Line 434: "Production waits for someone to test the preview before it deploys." These ids are unpublished, so there's no Answer history to lose: `git show main:content/lessons/08-pr-and-ship.md` has no test or checkpoint blocks.
quiz.fix:
Make it a real spot question:
```test spot-merge-then-test
On a recipe site set up like this one, a PR's migration renames the `ingredients` table. Sam clicks Squash and merge, then opens the preview to check the rename worked. Spot the mistake.
- [ ] Nothing: a revert undoes a migration like any other change.
  > Reverting the code doesn't undo what a migration did to the database. That's what can make it a one-way door.
- [x] The merge already ran the migration on the real database.
  > Right. Merging deploys production, and that build migrates the real database. Check the preview first, while a mistake only hits its copy.
- [ ] Nothing: production waits until someone has tested the preview.
  > Nothing waits. Merging to `main` deploys production straight away, migration included.
- [ ] Squash and merge skips migrations, so Sam must run this one by hand.
  > Squashing only combines the commits. The production build still runs the migration.
```

The Lesson has no step or clause that shows the diff locally. The reader lens assumes someone who barely uses Git, and `git diff` opens a pager they may not know how to leave.
reader.fix: Line 275: "Read it as the reviewer: Merge Danger first, then Evidence, then Summary. Ask the agent \"Show me the diff between this branch and main\" and check the door call against it. Then ask: ...". Line 199, at the end of the bullet: "Ask the agent to show you the diff, and check the call against it."

reader.where: How a change ships, line 39: "Vercel, which builds and hosts the site ... Every build also runs any **migration**"; Why it matters, line 24: "the pull request that added Comments to this site"
reader.problem: Two terms reach a cold reader without a clause. "Build" as a noun (turning the code into the running site) is never explained. The Lesson later uses "build" to mean writing the feature as well (line 201 "before you build", line 441 "ready to build"). "Comments", a site feature with a capital C, is also never explained.
reader.evidence: No clause explains "build" at line 39 or anywhere else in the Lesson. GLOSSARY.md defines **Comment** as "A note a Visitor leaves on one Lesson", but the Lesson never says what a Comment is. Line 111 only says what `body` and `name` mean.
reader.fix: Line 39: "Vercel, which builds the site (turns its code into the running website) and hosts it, builds a **preview** of every branch you push...". Line 24: "Picture the pull request that added Comments (notes readers leave under a Lesson) to this site."

reader.where: Goals, line 17: "use that to decide how hard to review and when to test before merging"
reader.problem: The goal says the door call helps decide when to test before merging. The Lesson itself says you always test on the preview first: "you test on the preview before you merge, never after" (line 69). It also teaches the door as deciding only how hard to review (lines 143, 198 and 229). A cold reader gets two different rules.
reader.evidence: Line 69: "That's why ==you test on the preview before you merge==, never after". spot-merge-then-test (line 433) marks merging before testing as the mistake whatever the door.
reader.fix: Line 17: "- You'll be able to judge whether a change can be undone (a two-way door) or not (a one-way door), use that to decide how hard to review, and say why testing on the preview always comes before the merge."
